articleTitle: A systems dynamics case study of competing optical storage technologies under market uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Interacting technologies are the result of innovation and can be considered as complex systems. Technology is then the result of innovation. These interactions between technologies are typically time dependant and are modeled here using systems dynamics. The effect of uncertain market conditions in the case of competing laser optical storage technology systems is specifically discussed as part of a systems dynamics case study using triangular distributions. The Lotka-Volterra approach is used to model the interaction between the two technology systems. This work is based on previous work on the substitution of red laser diode technology by blue laser technology in optical storage systems.

articleTitle: Using ANP, VIKOR, and dematel for holistic knowledge management of SMEs
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Most SMEs are suffering because of low profits caused by hyper competition and OEM dead-end. Moreover, since the middle of 2008, the financial tsunami has caused serious damage to the global economy. They lack the financial and systematic basis to introduce knowledge management practices and make innovations. Several researchers have explored the gaps in the knowledge management activities of enterprises. Their studies reveal that corporate performance is significantly influenced by those gaps. This paper proposes a Group Decision Approach for making strategic decisions about knowledge management adoption. Our research aimed to clarify the misunderstanding of high expenditure on knowledge management systems adoption, and provided a novel approach for the most emergent knowledge management components to catch up the paces of their rival for the late adopter of knowledge management systems.

articleTitle: Combinatorial optimization design and operating management mechanisms for logistics supply chain management
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: For improved competitiveness, many modern firms have embraced the supply chain management to increase organizational effectiveness and achieve such organizational goals as improved customer value, better utilization of resources, and increased profitability. One main issue of logistics supply chain management is to find suitable optimized design mechanisms when a corporation decides to open and operate its warehouses and cross-docks and expend huge financial sums to open its best set of cross-docks and warehouses, the other main issue of logistics supply chain management is the effective operating management of the logistical supply chain processes that are controlled by various independent companies in order to achieve overall minimal cost after the corporation had opened and operated its warehouses and cross-docks. Suitable combinatorial optimized logistics supply chain design mechanisms and effective operating management method are considered for the problems of the logistics supply chain management in this paper.

articleTitle: Developing a Knowledge Management framework based on Km cycle in non-profit educational centers: A multi case analysis
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper intends to develop a framework for knowledge management cycle in some non-profit educational centers (NPEC) in Iran. So, a Delphi panel was designed, applied and then analyzed for developing the framework based on KM (Knowledge Management) cycle. The suggested framework for KM cycle in NPECs includes Knowledge sharing, Knowledge storage, Knowledge identification, Knowledge organizing, Knowledge collecting, Knowledge management evaluation, and Preparation and infrastructures as the important factors.

articleTitle: Prognostic health management for environmental monitoring
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The effect of environmental pollution has caused an increased in chronic and communicable diseases. Substantial efforts have been devoted to identifying the factors. An array of sensors is required to monitor various environmental conditions, such as temperature, humidity, pollutant presence, motion, intrusion, and vibration. When a sensor goes out of range of a configurable threshold, monitoring will be suspended. Prognostics and system health management is an effective technique to provide condition-based monitoring for ensuring reliability and availability for an environmental monitoring system.

articleTitle: N/MEMS R&D technology strategy and management
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: MEMS and nanotechnology have become significant new technologies in just the past 15 years. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has provided key research and development funding for both academic and industrial laboratories that has driven new research directions and commercial products. DARPA's experience has identified five management of technology themes that have defined the evolution of the MEMS research and development and commercial communities. These same themes are directly applicable in the exciting new and still emerging field of nanotechnology.

articleTitle: Economics of infrastructure management and selective sourcing
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper presents a services model for management of IT infrastructure based on the core-actual-augmented (CAA) framework. This model allows simplification, categorisation and prioritisation of investments that enhance strategic agility with respect to business goals. The economic competitive market model is then used to analyse feasibility of outsourcing the prioritized IT investments to the market. It is shown that, it is uneconomical to the value of the Dead-Weight-Loss (DWL) for an organization to outsource its assets to the market, unless all internal efficiencies in the form of economies of scale, scope, management and organizational process flows have been optimized to full potential where possible.

articleTitle: On the concentration of productivity and impact in science and technology
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: As the productivity and impact of papers and patents have increased in recent years, this study attempts to explore whether the productivity and impact from academic research and technology are concentrated on a few countries by analysis with various indicators, namely HHI. This study finds the papers and patents are in fact concentrated on a few countries, but the concentration rate has declined over the years. The patent concentration is higher than paper concentration and decreases at a slower rate in compared to papers, even if United States is excluded from the analysis. The distribution of papers and patents are more dispersed through the years. The study also finds a correlation between the distribution of papers/patents and the GDP of a country, while population is only correlated with paper productivity. In analysis that excluded United States, the correlation results are similar in the case of patents.

articleTitle: New inventory model for perishable valuable materials such as special diseases' drugs
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Inventory control models for perishable materials of different industries especially chemical, food and medicinal industries are very sensitive. Since drugs ingredients are mostly organic compounds and effective application of them in medications depend on appropriate stability level, the way drug compounds decayed follow chemical stability functions. In this research, at first, the drug products deteriorate function is studied and then an inventory model for medicinal products with drug deteriorate function is presented in order to obtain the least cost considering shortage of backlogging. Demand rate depending on inventory level is modeled in three levels: one producer, two distributors and six buyers. Finally, optimum of drug supply chain model costs is studied and compared in two modes of integrated and non-integrated.

articleTitle: Three essential factors toward achievement of green supply chain environment
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Building a green supply chain environment is one of the most important responsibilities of every government in a country. This logistics flows from materials procurement to distribution activities. Three important factors have to be paid special attention to attain the green environment. In case they are applied in a good manner, the hope of achieving a green environment is increased. These steps are the logical rules and regulations, an effective information system and a developed general conscience of the people. In this paper, these three items are investigated in detail. It has been clearly shown that the top management of every country has the main responsibility in practicing the green environment. These three factors should be applied together and the lack of just one of them will render the process incomplete.

articleTitle: Improvement of the supply chain system for cooked chicken product exported to Japan: a case study in Thailand for this industry
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Due to the complexity of food supply chain management, it is difficult to determine precise areas requiring improvement. This paper aims to develop a key problem identification and extraction framework, based on value stream mapping and theory of constraint techniques for food supply chain improvement direction. A case study in Thailand's cooked chicken industry was used to illustrate to this. It is essential to identify and understand the main problems of this chain by focusing on the effects from downstream to upstream and finding opportunities to solve defects. The results indicate that a non-value added step more than 90% at the processing factory and caused a bottleneck in capacity resource analysis which revealed main problem.

articleTitle: Service valuation in business and IT alignment: with a case study in banking in China
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In business and IT alignment, the implementation of IT is determined by business objectives and its services. In order to help organizations invest wisely in IT and makes the best use of the current facilities, this paper aims to deliver a method for assessing the value of service in business and IT Alignment. The method provides specific guideline in service evaluation process and assesses value based on the perspectives of stakeholders. This study is carried out under Business Aligned IT Strategy (BAITS) architecture and extends the original valuation framing method, which is also considered as a contribution to the organizational semiotics. Finally, the paper validates the approach by involving a case study in banking in China.

articleTitle: Human resource management innovation based on the view of knowledge management
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: It's acknowledged that development of human resource management innovation can be facilitated by knowledge management. Therefore, companies should understand the relationship between knowledge management and human resource management innovation and the combination of two components which can realize human capital value.

articleTitle: An expert based view on the decreased quality of the Dutch innovation system. Applying the ‘functions of innovation systems’-approach
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: A sound innovation policy is key for Dutch policy makers since its national innovativeness is decreasing according to several international studies. Based on in-depth interviews with 15 Dutch innovation-experts several findings were identified that explain the decreased Dutch innovativeness: e.g., a low level of knowledge absorptive capacity by Dutch companies and a preference of Dutch managers for cost cutting measures instead of innovating. We related these findings to the `functions of innovation systems'-approach. Based on the findings different suggestions for improvement of the Dutch innovativeness were formulated. For instance: establishing a Ministry of Innovation, and setting up a revolving fund for great ideas to mobilize more resources for innovation and assure diffusion of research to practice.

articleTitle: A risk management-based decision model for a type of dynamic multi-state systems with application on maritime transportation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In this paper, a framework for risk analysis of dynamic multi-state weighted k-out-of-n systems is presented by combining Markov process and Universal Generating Function. The uncertainties in the system demand were considered and optimal management decision is made based on achieved risk and system cost. The use of this approach is illustrated on a case of maritime transportation, which generated promising results on system availability and optimal design.

articleTitle: Developing smart and active packaging of inventory model in drug supply chain for special diseases
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: At a outset, active and smart packaging and their role in supply chain is studied, then by means of special function of drug products decay for completing the model in order to investigate the role of active and smart packaging in decay rate and service level of medicinal products, a coefficient is added to the model as smart packaging factor and then evaluating it. After that, an inventory model for medicinal products with drug decay function is presented in order to obtain the least cost considering shortage of backlogging. Demand rate depending on inventory level is modeled in three levels. Finally, to specify the role of packaging, optimum of drug supply chain model costs is studied.

articleTitle: Planning and implementation of large scale enterprise data center: The Case of China National Petroleum Company
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This article made an approach to information planning and engineering management via business analysis, system architecture, technology planning, and project management, meanwhile, combined with the case of China National Petroleum Company Data Center Project, it also expounded some key issues that large-scale enterprise information system project implementation process should pay attention to. The China National Petroleum Company's enterprise data center planning & implementation, adopted information engineering methodology and project life circle as theoretical guide, conformed to international/Chinese domestic related standards, as well as established its own characteristic management model. Originality and value: In this paper, other Chinese and foreign enterprises with large-scale data center planning & implementation may obtain some valuable references.

articleTitle: The influencing factors of disruptive innovation in China's high-tech SMEs: A case study
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In this paper we proposed four main factors influencing disruptive innovation, government support, external knowledge resources, strategy orientation and research position in SMEs. We also provided theoretical model and evidence from a case study on SXF Technology Co., Ltd how disruptive innovation helped firms to gain competitive advantage quickly and how disruptive innovation created a favorable market performance. We also put forward some suggestions to SMEs in every dimension.

articleTitle: A comparative study on manufacturing strategy of Chinese and German manufacturer
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Globalization leads to the movement of companies towards international cooperation in manufacturing. Manufacturing strategy (MS) is one of the most important issues for manufacturing companies to secure sustainable advantage. It is imperative for companies to understand the manufacturing strategy of their international cooperators to ensure cooperation success. In the last decades, more and more Sino-German cooperative Manufacturing has been occurred. China differs from Germany in a number of aspects such as economy, institution and social culture. Based on an empirical study, this paper compares the manufacturing strategies in relation to the manufacturing objective and practice between Chinese and Germany industry and the background for the differences is discussed.

articleTitle: Outsourcing of R&D: Chances and risks
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The possibility of outsourcing business activities, especially in the fields of IT and manufacturing has attracted attention from both practitioners and academia. Yet literature addressing issues of outsourcing research and development (R&D) activities remains rather limited. This paper focuses on the chances and risks of R&D outsourcing by analyzing critical success factors. Firstly, we define R&D outsourcing, and provide a framework for analysis. Next, we discuss our small-scale preliminary empirical study based on expert telephone interviews in which relevant factors that influence the success of outsourcing were investigated, focusing on chances and risks. The results, supplemented by literature analysis, provide preliminary findings that could be used by firms from different industries in their decisions on R&D outsourcing.

articleTitle: Performance management of academic staff in the Faculty of Economics and Business Administration at Tartu University (pluses and minuses)
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The present study aims to establish the pluses and minuses of the performance appraisal and management system of the academic staff. This is done through the case study of the Faculty of Economics and Business Administration (FEBA) at Tartu University, Estonia. Research is based on the analysis of quantitative and qualitative research methods. The author carried out document analysis and two original questionnaires in the FEBA. In order to achieve this aim, the author questioned the academic staff during the years of 2004–2007. The author carried out 5 semi-structured focus interviews with senior management and lecturers and 10 individual interviews between the years of 2004–2009. The author of this article took part in all these processes, including the expert groups and board, and applied the participation observation method where appropriate.

articleTitle: Investment allocation in innovation resources in open innovation: a research in Chinese power equipment manufacturing firms
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This study has examined the connection of activities in innovation related resource management and the profit status due to technological innovation based on a sample 219 firms in Chinese power equipment manufacturing industry. We have taken correlation and regression analysis to test the impact of different activities on 3 types of innovation. The result has provided us with the key activities which have the most significant impact on innovation performances, in which we found a strange mode of technology introduction employed by the firms which results from the capability and resource shortage of the firms. In reference to the result, we have made propositions to help Chinese power equipment manufactories in achieving higher efficient technology introduction and radical innovation promoted by market pull.

articleTitle: Forking, leadership control and social capital in open innovation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Open innovation, by sponsoring communities of knowledge contributors, has attracted the attention of business firms as it can help generate diverse ideas to innovate new products. This paper draws attention to forking within communities, whereby sub-groups form and pursue agendas different from the overall community's goals. While forking can sometimes be beneficial, it can also harm the community by disrupting its integrity and in turn, threaten the interests of the sponsoring firm. It is argued the increasing leadership control can help reduce the likelihood of forking up to a certain point, beyond which it might again increase forking possibility. Increasing social capital in the community can help reduce the likelihood of forking for a given level of leadership control. This paper offers propositions, and highlights the need for further research in this area.

articleTitle: An international comparative study of funds supporting for independent innovation and countermeasures of China
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Based on open data of U.S., Japan, Korea, Chinese, we do a comparative study of external funds support for Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) independent innovation. We find that there are varying degrees of problems in promoting independent innovation in China, especially financial system is still not fully play its role in risk diversification and sharing. Strength of the government is still small, relevant policies are not sound, input growth is relatively slow, need to increase its efforts to support independent innovation. To aim at these problems, we respectively put forward two specific strategies and optimization tips, which could strengthen government policy and perfect financial system.

articleTitle: Correspondence between manufacturing strategy paradigms and Wheelwright and Hayes model: Two case studies
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Competence in manufacturing can be assessed in dimensions such as cost, quality, delivery speed, delivery reliability, flexibility and innovation. Manufacturing strategy literature refers to three paradigms of competence building in manufacturing namely, trade-off, cumulative and integrative. It is likely that companies depending upon their strategic orientation use different approaches of competency building. A widely accepted four-stage model due to Wheelwright and Hayes (W-H) provides basis for assessing strategic role of manufacturing. This paper conducts an exploratory study using cases of two firms to investigate the correspondence between approaches of competency building and stages of W-H model.

articleTitle: Incorporating business value models into organic e-farming system
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper describes an intellectual organic farming system surrounding the organic authentication center based on three business value models: value chain, value shop, and value network, to create high-end agricultural businesses in the era of the Internet and environmentalism. This system further handles four types of value sources of e-business: efficiency, complementarities, lock-in, and novelty, in order to elaborate the sustainable competitive functions of an agricultural e-business. Finally, the authors illustrate a conceptual framework, including related functional deployment of e-farming value chain, value shop, and value network, to articulate the intellectual farming system with the competences of competitive advantage, knowledge management, and business scalability.

articleTitle: Patents and economic development in South Africa: Managing intellectual property rights
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Intellectual property rights systems are important policy instruments in the armoury of governments. They have the potential to have favourable or adverse consequences for the relevant national system of innovation, technology transfer, research and development and eventually economic growth. While there is a substantial debate related to the optimization of patent systems in the developed world, there is limited debate related to the approaches used in developing countries like South Africa. This article presents an effort to assess whether the South African non-examining patent system makes a contribution or it is detrimental to the country's development. We find that the current intellectual property rights regime not only does not support the objectives of the national innovation system but it facilitates exploitation by foreign interests and creates substantial social costs.

articleTitle: The effect of compensation satisfaction on performance
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This study mainly discusses the influence of job involvement, job stress, and compensation satisfaction on the job performance of stock dealers' salespeople when conducting financial cross-selling sales. We sent out a total of 380 questionnaires, and retrieved 244 valid ones. Using regression analysis statistics to test the hypotheses shows that compensation satisfaction is a significant and positive influence on job involvement in salespeople's financial cross-selling; the more job involvement is, the more performance is. Job stress are negatively influence on compensation satisfaction; job stress are significantly and positively influence on job performance. Lastly, compensation satisfaction are significantly and positively influence on job performance.

articleTitle: A theoretical study on interactive innovation and innovation capability building of SMEs
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Innovation is a process full of interaction. The innovation system needs the collaboration among different organizations in the interactive process of knowledge creation, diffusion and application. However what interactive innovation does to the development of innovation capability? It's still a question under research. This paper is going to find a solution to this research question from theoretical perspective by taking SMEs as research objective. Based on literature review and archival analysis of interaction, process innovation and innovation capability, this paper develops an integrated conceptual model on the relationship between interactive innovation and innovation capability building and provides some propositions on the innovation capability building for SMEs.

articleTitle: Corporate environmentalism in emerging markets: Lessons from a country in transition
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In order to find out what is the state of corporate environmentalism in Slovenia, a country in transition, we surveyed a large sample of Slovenian manufacturing companies. Our results show that none of the identified company clusters exhibits qualities attributed to fully advanced corporate environmentalism. In such circumstances regulatory pressures and top management's personal preferences still play a major role in motivating corporate environmentalism.

articleTitle: How does Chinese technology policy work: A co-evolutionary analysis
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper builds a co-evolution framework to study the interaction and evolution mechanism of Chinese technology policy. Based on the analysis of multiple principal-agent relationships, multiple games among central governments, local governments and enterprises; it shows the co-evolution mechanism of central technology policy, local technology policy and enterprises' technology strategy. It is the complexity of economic and technological conditions, agent problems, Information asymmetry, and conspiracy between governance agents and enterprises at certain extent under certain environment lead to the feverish interest to technology introduction and FDI, serious absence of absorption, and then mislead Chinese technology policy.

articleTitle: Science as a tool for commercialization: A case of Kaneka's development of the solar business
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: With growing public concern about environmental issues, solar photovoltaics is becoming one of the most promising industries. The solar battery or solar cell module is a key device for this industry. Japanese solar cell manufacturers have been at the forefront in the progress of this technology. Most of these companies are electronics manufacturers, such as Sanyo electronics, Sharp, and Kyocera. Although Kaneka is one of these companies, it manufactures chemicals. How did Kaneka venture into this industry and build their competitiveness? This study analyzes its new business creation process. The results of this study show that science was Kaneka's key success factor. The paper proposes a new perspective on science as a tool for commercial innovation.

articleTitle: Exponential improvements and increasing returns to scale
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper uses the concepts of “increasing returns to scale” (IRtS) and nested hierchies of subsystems (NHoS) to explain the sources and implications of exponential improvements. IRtS exists to a greater extent in some technologies than in other technologies and realizing the benefits from IRtS often depends on the performance and cost of lower level “components” in system's NHOS. On the other hand, when a component has a large impact on the cost and performance of a system and when the component exhibits increasing returns over a broad range of scale, the IRtS in the component can drive exponential improvements in the cost and performance of the system.

articleTitle: An analysis of the net efficiency of Korea's national R&D programs
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper assesses the net efficiency of Korea's government-sponsored R&D projects using a threestage approach. Measuring its net efficiency raises the reliability of the analysis results by increasing the homogeneity of DMUs. The empirical results show that the private participation has a positive effect on the R&D efficiency. This implies the necessity of efforts to encourage private organizations to participate aggressively in the R&D programs. This study expects to contribute to formulating policy for efficient operation of the R&D programs.

articleTitle: Technology assessment as guidance to foreign direct investment in telecom industry between Taiwan and Russia
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Telecom industry is the fundamental industry of a nation, and it is also another vital business, along with WTO, the wave of globalization, and government's policy. The entire telecom market becomes a fair and fully competitive market environment, and in order to develop telecom industry, the technology assessment has become an important procedure. It consists technology development and its consequences, provides valuable information to help decision makers make strategies. The purpose of this study aims at forming sophisticated model of considering internal, and external factors by the consideration under comparative advantage as well as the industrial development and competitive market conditions; providing a valuable framework to entrepreneurs of foreign direct investment (FDI) in decision making, and use Taiwan telecom development as background to compare with Russia telecom market.

articleTitle: Making the un-transactional transactional: A case study in foundry industry
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Collaborative commerce has become a competitive weapon in the virtual world. However, there is little empirical evidence on the effect of collaborative commerce in reducing inter-company transaction costs within the Transaction Cost Economy (TCE) theory. This paper analyzes the practical case of company A in the semiconductor foundry industry to reduce un-transactional factors and facilitate transactional commerce. The results indicate that collaborative commerce has a significant impact on reducing monitoring, searching and contracting costs, while playing a more modest role in reducing enforcement costs.

articleTitle: Innovation policies in fast- growing countries. Lessons for Mexico
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In the first part of the article we deal with the main concepts relating to the innovation systems and we further illustrate some remarkable systems of innovation on account of its efficacy given the definition of strategies and supporting areas allowing for the shaping of several policy aspects. Finally, we set forth a series of guidelines on good policy practices and elements that must be taken into account to define the innovation policy in Mexico.

articleTitle: The risk reducing effect of forecasting in supply chains
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In order to realise just-in-time concepts in supply chains, customers usually have to provide information about their required materials to their suppliers. Now the problem arises what forecast data the customer should report to his suppliers when the future demand of his outlet is not exactly known. This demand usually is subject to a probability distribution. Without any restrictions, the customer will always report those forecast data that correspond to the possible maximum demand of his outlet in order to keep flexibility. This information will not be useful to the supplier. Therefore, the customer usually is engaged to purchase, within certain limitation periods, that quantity of parts he reported. Otherwise he has to do an adjustment payment. This paper analyses what forecast data the customer should report, which amount the supplier should take into consideration in light of the customer's intentions and what release order quantity the customer should realise having previously reported the forecast data.

articleTitle: Strategic heuristic and valuation of defence R&D investments: A real options approach
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: A strategic objective of defence R&D investments is the development of the indigenous defence technological capabilities, and the R&D process can be viewed as a capability development process. This paper builds on the literature in technology management and real options theory and presents a framework for defence R&D investments as real options. Defence R&D projects could be treated as one of three types of real options, depending on their degree of technical and application uncertainty. Positioning options are application driven technological options in specific capabilities and offers the opportunity to compete in some future and still unclear technological arena. Scouting options are used to learn about the operational scenario by probing or offering prototypes to potential early adopters. Stepping-stone options are broad-based options which can be framed as a generic set of resources and form platforms for future development and opportunities. Applications of this framework for strategic heuristic and a methodology for the valuation of the real options are discussed.

articleTitle: Hidden motives: Knowledge-sharing problems in supply chain collaboration
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Effective knowledge management relies on the premise of organizational members to be willing to contribute what they know. However, it is not unusual to find that employees are not willing to share knowledge with each other, even when such sharing brings substantial benefits. Current literature investigates largely the explicit and implicit motives that inhibit knowledge sharing. However, we often neglect the hidden motives which are socially ascribed in members' collaborative activities. This article identifies four hidden motives that hinder engineers' cross-boundary collaboration and the use of information systems. Our study further investigates how these hidden motives bring about knowledge-sharing dilemmas and unscrupulous behaviors. Theoretical and practical implications are discussed.

articleTitle: The mechanism of technological innovation in local industrial clusters: The case of specialized town economy in Guangdong
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In this paper, we will discuss how local industrial clusters build up a technological innovation system and its operating mechanism. Based on case study, we developed a “Four-in-One” model of technological innovation in Guangdong specialized towns to analyze the mechanism of technological innovation in industrial clusters. We also found that the innovation center plays an important role in enhancing the competitiveness of industrial clusters and of the regional economy.

articleTitle: Innovation and information technology in virtual organizations: An empirical study
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Research concerning innovation management by definition involves multilevel analysis. Focusing on the innovation at individual and organizational levels, this study examines the intensity of the relationship between individual creativity and organizational innovation to identify the construct of innovation composition process across these two levels. Due to a shift in organizational change management, which exceeds the convenience of advanced information technologies (IT), this study identifies and analyzes the effect of virtual organizational (VO) structure on the interaction between individual creativity and organizational innovation. Through the regression analysis of 128 information and electronic companies in Taiwan, the results show that the adoption of VO positively influences organizational innovation. Furthermore, it positively moderates the relationship between individual creativity and organizational innovation.

articleTitle: An investigation of process innovation activity levels and their influencing factors in two Irish manufacturing facilities
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Process innovation has come into sharper focus in recent years with the demand of increased global competition coupled with recessionary effects. This paper reviews the difference between two separate manufacturing factories of a large multinational corporation within the ICT sector, both equally exposed to the recession. It specifically examines the level of process innovation along with the main influencing factors that were identified by two large manufacturing facilities and sets out a set of management propositions that support sustainable process innovation. For confidentiality reasons the factories will be referred to as Westport and Southport.

articleTitle: The impact of motivation on employee innovative behavior and the disparity analysis: An empirical study of Zhejiang Province in China
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In this study, we developed and tested a model of total motivation systems by integrating internal motivation, awards and rewards, organizational innovative climate to analyze the effect of these systems on employee innovative behavior, and then analyzed the disparity of different groups classified by academic degree, age, and job post. Three hundred and fifty three employees from high technology industries of Zhejiang Province in China participated in the study, and we collected data using a survey questionnaire. As hypothesized, the results of regression analysis suggested that internal motivation, awards and rewards, organizational innovative climate were significantly and positively related to employee innovative behavior, and there was a positive and significant interaction effect between internal motivation and awards and rewards. The results also showed that there were significant disparities of impact among different groups. Implications are discussed.

articleTitle: Complementary versus competitive convergence: the Case of the French IPTV and VoD market
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In this paper, we analyse the evolution of the VoD and TV supply in France, and in particular the effect of the launch of IPTV systems. Firstly, the launch of attractive triple-play offers has induced a strong development of the French broadband Internet access market, which in turn has resulted in the entry of numerous players in the VoD market. Secondly, the adoption of IPTV system has changed the competitive and strategic positioning of main players in the VoD value-chain, thus inducing or amplifying strategic moves along this value-chain. In particular, we show how the diffusion of IPTV systems has induced a switch from complementary convergence to competitive convergence.

articleTitle: Belonging in the team, or chosen to be in the ‘in-group’ of the supervisor - which promotes more discretionary effort?
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper looks at the ideas associated with discretionary effort (DE). It uses a case study approach, with the theory of Leader-Member Exchange (LMX) and the LMX-7 questionnaire to assess the relationships in two teams at a Slovenian manufacturing organization. Results show that, contrary to the LMX theory, more DE is created by the relationships between team members, than by developing the high level relationships with the supervisor. Implications for the future will be to cultivate the within team relationships while strengthening the relationships with the supervisor, to allow for a synergistic effect, where DE, such as continuous improvement (CI) programs, becomes part of the in-role tasks.

abstract: The following topics are dealt with: technology strategy management; technology forecasting; healthcare; project management; supply chain management; intellectual property; innovation management; investment; six sigma; quality management; R&D management;sustainable development; environmental management; service innovation; product development; product design; human capital; innovation policy; knowledge management; manufacturing strategy; system design engineering; IT management; e-commerce; and risk management.

publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Research on the co-evolution of industrial cluster development and entrepreneur learning based on knowledge capitalization
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Based on the approach of coevolution symbiosis and focusing on the mutual promotion of cluster development and entrepreneurial activity, the paper takes the lead to carry out a systemic study on entrepreneur and industry cluster from a microscopic perspective. It is pointed out in the paper that the symbiosis relationship between industry cluster and entrepreneur not only gives an impetus to entrepreneurial activity, but also prompts a transformation of knowledge spillover into a driving force behind the development of whole cluster. First, a rotary model is constructed to analyze the interaction between industry cluster based on knowledge capitalization and entrepreneurial activities. Then, an empirical study is carried out on statistics about 53 high-tech industry clusters in China to examine how knowledge learning activities impact on entrepreneurial activities through global knowledge linkages and local knowledge linkages.

articleTitle: A study on green based collaborative product design
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The study integrates the network system with the concept and methodology of collaborative product design to enhance the customization and operation efficiency of new product designs. On the other hand, the perspectives of green product design are also introduced into the corporation to serve as the best tool for creating innovation and improving competitiveness.

articleTitle: Distance Reading Education
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper is about a framework that would promote distance education in the Philippines. Its focus is on the development of reading comprehension among primary elementary school age Filipinos in the remote barrios where access to free education is not available. Modern technology such as mobile or satellite phones, solar power and internet will make this framework work in rural areas. Another important component is the willingness of the stakeholders to cooperate and support the project implementation. This paper hopes to contribute to the primary education strategy of developing countries like the Philippines to uplift the lives of their citizens especially in the rural communities.

articleTitle: An effective content-based web image searching engine algorithm
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper provides an effective content-based web image searching engine based on SIFT (Scale Invariant Feature Transform) feature matching. SIFT descriptors, which are invariant to image scaling and transformation and rotation, and partially invariant to illumination changes and affine, present the local features of an image. To decrease unavailable features matching, a dynamic probability function replaces the original fixed value to determine the similarity distance and database from training images. Then, by using pretreatment of the source images, the keypoints will be stored to the XML format, which can improve the searching performance. Finally, the results displayed to the user through the HTML. The experimental results show that this method improves the stability and precision of image searching engine.

articleTitle: Design process gene in product development
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Process of product design bears analogies with the process of biological evolution. Based on this viewpoint, this paper introduces the notion of biologic heritability and mutation into product design process management. The paper presents the concept of design process gene and also discloses that the structure of design process gene is made up of an ordered sequence of pairs of design process bases. The composition of four design process bases and six pairs of design process bases are analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: The best practice agile e-CRM framework based on House of Quality
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: It is imperative to respond to the voice of the customer (VOC) and the priorities of customers' requirements when implementing e-Business strategies. On the other hand, the House of Quality (HOQ) is a tool that translates the VOC into measurable design targets and a set of engineering specifications. The purpose of this paper is to determine the best practice agile e-customer relationship management (e-CRM) framework that meets customer requirements. The proposed model applies House of quality tool to recognize these customer needs and expectations and satisfy throughout the entire e-Business process. We present a novel structured framework to select the best practice agile e-CRM framework to take advantage of the rapid changes in the business environment before its implementation.

articleTitle: Key component supplier supports based on product complexity during New Product Development - A case study of Netbook PC manufacturers in Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The process of New Product Development (NPD) involves several stages, each involving different problems. Efficiently solving these problems requires support from key component suppliers. This study, based on different levels of product complexity, classifies innovative products into two types, low complexity and high complexity, and uses Netbook PC (small notebook PC) as a case study to conduct a full product comparison of six product types. This study shows that manufacturers should seek various forms of supplier support when encountering problems during the NPD process. Furthermore, in the case of products with high complexity, more diversified marketing and technology support are required from key component suppliers.

articleTitle: Evaluation of shuttle bus lines for the high-speed rail by using analytic hierarchy process
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: High speed rail and buses are public transportation systems and possess the attribute of sustainable environment. A well-developed process for deciding bus lines, which are integrated with high speed rail, is essential for sustainable development. This study proposes an evaluation framework for shuttle bus lines with three evaluation dimensions and eleven evaluation indexes by adopting the Tainan high speed rail station as a case study. A questionnaire based on the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is designed to interview with bus operators, scholars and public transportation authorities. By applying AHP, this study elicits interviewee opinions on evaluation indexes and analyzes the weight of each index. Results indicate that travel time, travel cost and bus schedule are significant evaluation indicators for shuttle bus lines. With respect to the priority of shuttle bus lines, lines 1, 3 and 4 rank as the leading three places based on the weighted sum of performance values.

articleTitle: A competition model of bilateral platform enterprise with overlapping business
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Based on the Hotelling Model, this paper construct an overlapping business competition model about bilateral platform enterprise. Focusing on the platform of two situations that one is single attribution while the other is multipartite attribution. This study analyzed both the existence and the structure of the equilibrium solution, and three main conclusions were drawn up. Finally, the study tested these findings through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A study of designing around patents based on Function Trimming
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: In the era of knowledge-based economy, the patent barriers are getting more and more serious for enterprises when they enter the market, the space for the development of their technology is getting smaller and smaller. Resultantly designing around patents is particularly important. Therefore systematically innovative methods are badly needed to guide the enterprises to achieve better avoiding effects. This paper will combines the rules of patent infringement judgment with the modes of Function-trimming and construct an integrated process for designing around patents though Function Trimming in TRIZ and patent infringement judgment. And it greatly increases the possibility of design-around. Redesign of the spiral bevel gear milling machine to design around an existing patent is used to illustrate the integrated process.

articleTitle: Using tacit knowledge in organizational change: A case study of the Swedish model of management in Singapore
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: As a result of greater individual mobility, international organizations face the challenge of creating, harvesting, managing and retaining employee knowledge effectively. This study focuses on the use of tacit knowledge by Swedish managers in order to direct Swedish managed Singapore subsidiaries effectively. The concept of knowledge in this paper is situated in interpretive discourse, working with the assumption that knowledge is socially constructed, embedded in social and cultural contexts. The purpose of this study is two-fold, (i) to show how Swedish managers in Singapore leverage their tacit knowledge in the form of the Swedish management model to implement organizational changes, and (ii) to outline the effects of the use of the Swedish management model in Singapore on creating, harvesting and the retaining of knowledge within the organization. The methods of analysis employed are grounded theory and discourse analysis on long interviews.

articleTitle: Deciding optimal center locations in a supply chain network
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This study explores how an enterprise selects locations of manufacturing centers and assembling/distribution centers by focusing on an enterprise that supplies inbound demand for the domestic market. A conventional supply chain network model is proposed to analyze the optimal manufacturing centers, optimal assembling/distribution centers, and their transporting volumes. A numerical example is proposed to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model. Results of the study demonstrate that approximately optimal transporting volume, which originates from the same nodes, should be equalized to subsequent and connected nodes for minimizing the total cost function of an enterprise.

articleTitle: Grey assessment model of risks in ship pilotage
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: By analyzing the module and concrete items of risks in ship pilotage, applying Grey theory analysis, brings forward the Grey Theory Analysis Model in ship pilotage risks analysis, Moreover, fuzzy function is taken in the analysis of relative risk factors, achieving the optimal relational coefficient of piloting risk factors, and finally obtaining the relational degree taxis. As indicated in the computing result of the model, Grey Relational Analysis can ensure results that are more practical.

articleTitle: New product promotion and E-commerce; effects of retailer webpage layout on buyer behavior
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This article studies effects of webpage layout in an online retailer on buyer behavior towards new products and is a sequel to a study performed by authors in department stores. Webpage layout -in terms of parameters which influence buyer behavior- is formulated by two variables; pattern of prices and pattern of popularity. A novel method based on above-mentioned study, has been developed to measure these two factors, so that they can be compared against retailer sales statistics. Investigating this relationship helps both online retailers and marketing agents to better understand effect of webpage layout in promoting a newly developed product. Results show that correlation between price difference and department share is strong. There is a weak correlation between pick (popularity) difference and share from retailer sales. Finally we have tested prediction power of our model. A set of recommendations for webpage layout is developed based on the results of the research for marketing professionals.

articleTitle: A study on supplier evaluation in risk control based on food supply chain
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: To achieve food safety, risk control in food supply chain is required. Supplier evaluation and selection is one important process for food supply chain. This paper establishes a system based on risk control and integrates the DEA-based objective method and the ANP-based subjective method into a new ANP&DEA-based decision model for supplier evaluation. The paper explains the mathematical analysis in the specific case of a deteriorating food supply chain to confirm the model.

articleTitle: Applying scenario technology analysis for new product dynamic strategic planning
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This article intends to discuss the possibility of how to quickly improve the function of adaptive prediction direction for scenario analysis (SA) in technology-intensive industries. Therefore, this study is based on SA theory that combines the technology life cycle (TLC) viewpoint with the goal-oriented properties of path analysis model (PAM) to build an adapted SA for the purpose of dynamic technology forecasting. Using the goal-oriented properties of PAM, the adapted SA can quickly evaluate changes in the technical development of a market's dynamic schedule and can identify the gap between expectations and reality. This study proposes an adapted SA that allows the generation of both qualitative and quantitative scenarios that can be used as a helpful planning tool for dynamic assessment.

articleTitle: Strategic implications and consequences of pharmaceutical packaging of inhalers a study on Indian Doctors
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The Indian Pharmaceutical Industry will witness a very high growth rate. With a growing middle class sector having a huge spending power it is essential to understand the Indian market to offer the right marketing mix. It has been found by previous research that the packaging plays a vital role in the marketing strategy used by producers of Pharmaceuticals. This study analyses 400 Doctors in the four metro cities in India on the packaging functions for the inhaler formulation by adding on to the traditional packaging model providing valuable strategic inputs. The study shows the role of technology in the packaging of inhalers in order to formulate the appropriate marketing strategy.

articleTitle: International fishery supply chain risk management and insurance
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Supply chain is susceptible to a diverse set of risks for every company. In general terms, risks affecting a supply chain are related to the chance, in quantitative terms, of a defined hazard occurring. Supply chain risks involve probabilistic measures of the occurrences of particular events with an associated measure of the consequences of the events. Interest in supply chain management has also been growing in the international fishery industry both in developed and developing countries. Supply chains are increasingly vulnerable to catastrophic events such as hurricanes or terrorist attacks. Modern international fishery related company are more exposed to catastrophes and the result of their investments are made to operate supply chains with fewer human and capital resources. Along with the occurrence of several catastrophic events in international fishery supply chains, international fishery risk diversity and insurance problems become more and more important. In this paper, the problems of international international fishery supply chain risk management and insurance is considered.

articleTitle: A framework for determinants of transition from a manufacturer to a service provider
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Although a lot of literature emphasizes the benefits for a manufacturer to become a service provider, few describe the situation in which extending service is a good strategy. This paper has clearly differentiated service provider from manufacturers providing services by dividing the transition path into two stages. Then a model integrating factors of service strategy formulation and implementation is proposed, and a comparative cases analysis with replication logic is conducted to validate this model. Based on academic literatures and cases analyses, we concluded that not all manufacturers should adopt service strategy when confronting with intensive competitions, and that not all companies adopting service strategies can succeed, since appropriate organizational changes are critical.

articleTitle: Ethics of entrepreneurs in “China's Silicon Valley”—Zhongguancun
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper presents the results of a survey of entrepreneurial firms in the Zhongguancun early-stage incubator. Firms were asked about their knowledge on corporate ethics, self-description on ethical behavior. The results show that most of ZGC entrepreneurs regard corporate social responsibility as philanthropy donation and repaying to the society and motherland while making profit. Results also indicate that ZGC entrepreneurs are the group with high evaluation of themselves in ethics and believe that they needn't give up their ethics to succeed in their ventures. On the basis of this, self-actualization need of Chinese ZGC entrepreneurs, innate features of intellectual entrepreneurs, social expectation to them and government role are identified as key reasons for their ethical status.

articleTitle: International comparison of R&D investment on the basis of gray incidence theory
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The paper calculates the grey incidence degree of the Research and Development investment and Economic Development in some countries on the basis of the grey incidence theory in the main three performance sectors. The results demonstrate that the investment of science and technology talents is more important than R&D expenditure in promoting the development of economy. R&D expenditure gets higher degree of grey incidence in government performance sector than the researchers in China. The researcher input in business enterprise sector should be improved. To be supported by more R&D funds is necessary for the high education sector.

articleTitle: Modeling technological innovation capability as an engine of growth: Evidence from China's SMEs
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: With the advent of knowledge economies, technological innovation has assumed a critical role in business growth. The purpose of this paper is thus to investigate the impact of technological innovation capability on the growth of Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by establishing conceptual framework, distinguishing driving factors from various innovation attributes, and testing empirical models. Based on a national sample of 110 SMEs, this study reveals interesting results. First, the imbalance is obviously among input, output, and basis of innovation. Second, several factors of innovation input have direct effect on business growth. Third, increasing innovation input is the main pattern of improving technological innovation capability. The findings provide important propositions for innovation capability and the growth of SMEs.

articleTitle: Development of fuzzy clustering engine for decision making in manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage fuzzy clustering engine by combining fuzzy clustering method and fuzzy inference method. In the first stage, the raw data during manufacturing process can be classified based on its own nature, and with the classification results, operation decision can be made in the second stage by running fuzzy inference engine without relying on highly skilled expert. The objective of the proposed method eliminates the human interference so that the decision can be much more impersonal and reliable. In addition, to improve the performance, fuzzy rules in this engine are mostly derived from the natural feature of the raw data rather than the tradition fuzzy rules formalization. Also, a case study of a company based in Singapore has been presented, and the results are promising and satisfied by the company.

articleTitle: Open-Disruptive Innovation: An avenue for developing countries' independent innovation
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Developing countries focus on radical innovation naturally when they implement the technology innovation to catch up with Developed countries. However, recent studies have indicated a high rate of failures in the radical innovation. This paper illustrates the obstacles for developing countries to implement the radical innovation. Then we introduce a new innovation method - Open-Disruptive Innovation (ODI). With this method, we can obtain the technological resources from outside regularly and improve the core competitiveness effectively. Actually, many companies in China achieve success with this method. It is one of the best methods for Developing Countries to achieve the independent innovation. The paper cites two China's cases to verify ODI effective in enhancing the capability of independent innovation and also summarizes the law of the innovation practice.

articleTitle: Perspective main industry country innovation policy and innovation research performance of global
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Innovation is one of the most important fields in research and development of new services knowledge today, making innovation policy and Innovation research performance is an important issue. This study evaluates the main industry country innovation policy and innovation research performance of the past sixteen years. Data are based on the online version of SSCI, Web of Science from 1993 to 2008. The result displays that the USA is number one in innovation research totaling 6,317 papers, followed by UK totaling 2,354 papers. Other leading countries in innovation research include Canada, the Netherlands, Germany, France, Australia and Italy. This new bibliometric method can help researchers realize the panorama of worldwide innovation research, and establish further research direction.

articleTitle: Research of organizational RMS engineering capability assessment method
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The effective assessment of organizational reliability, maintainability and supportability (RMS) engineering capability has an important significance to improving organizational RMS work level. For the problem of organizational RMS engineering capability assessment being complex, and many indexes being fuzzy and difficult to be defined the value and weight, a method based on fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) was proposed to assess organizational RMS engineering capability. Firstly, the concept of organizational RMS engineering capability was defined and the index system for RMS engineering capability assessment was presented. Secondly, concrete steps of organizational RMS engineering capability assessment method based on FAHP for application of the system were introduced. Finally, the application of a case was given to verify the method effectively.

articleTitle: Investigating information technology adoption success: the influence of fit and trust
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper reports the results of a research project addressing the adoption success of an information technology application. Two main antecedents namely the fit of the process, technology and individual characteristics, and trust were tested to examine their influence to information technology adoption success. Using a survey, we found there are significant relationships between the antecedents and the success. Implications and future research suggestions are offered.

articleTitle: A study on corporate performance in TTQS introduction
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: As human capital is one of the most important elements of productivity in the era of knowledge economy, talent training has become the fundamental work for industries in development. Yet, while promoting the investment of business institutions in the human capital of their employees, it is more important to make efforts in ensuring training quality and performance so as to enhance the willingness and capability of the business institutions to give trainings, and further to upgrade the labors competitiveness. The Bureau of the Employment and Vocational Training, Executive Yuan, laid out the Taiwan TrainQuali System (TTQS), in respect to the stages of training, including plan, design, do, review and outcome, to ensure of the reliability and accuracy of training process.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-grey evaluation of product scheme based on QFD theory
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The aim of the current study is to implement fuzzy set theory and grey theory for selection of a proper scheme that will best meet customers requirements with uncertainty and lack of information. In the first phase, we propose a framework based on traditional quality function deployment (QFD). Analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is utilized to compute the transcendental weight. Then, entropy theory is used to achieve amendatory weight. In the next phase, the scheme evaluation model is put forward. The fuzzy logic and trapeziform fuzzy numbers are utilized to deal with vagueness of human thought and grey relational analysis is adopted to measure the relationship between objective sequence and reference sequences. Finally, a case study is conducted to illustrate the evaluation.

articleTitle: Improving PhD processes in management
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: One of the factors that can influence the economic status of countries is the education of the workforce. Improvements in education can positively impact economic growth. This paper is oriented on one program in particular, i.e. a PhD program in Industrial Engineering and Management with an emphasis on international issues. This program started in 1990 and recently more challenges with the quality of the research of PhD students were observed. This paper offers an exploratory analysis to determine key issues in the PhD program. It was concluded that many of the required skills should already be present in PhD students at the beginning of the PhD program in order to successfully complete it.

articleTitle: Improvement design of lithium battery explosion-proof equipment based on TRIZ and AFD
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: A process model of product improvement design based on anticipatory failure determination (AFD) and theory of resolving inventive problems (TRIZ) is put forward. In this model, AFD is used to find the problem that need to be solved in the system improvement design, and TRIZ is used to produce schemes for resolving problems. By applying the proposed method, homogeneity problem of the lithium battery explosion-proof equipment is resolved, and several schemes are put forward.

articleTitle: Level of supply chain collaboration of Malaysian SME manufacturers
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: The purpose of this research is to identify the level of supply chain collaboration of Malaysian SME manufacturers. This is determined by using the level of supply chain operational information integration with trading partners as an indicator to the level of supply chain collaboration. This study deployed both quantitative and qualitative approaches to identify the level of supply chain collaboration and explained why it is at the said level. The research discovered that the level of supply chain collaboration of Malaysian SME manufactures with their trading partners is at minimal level. This research also uncovered that the type of business relation intimacy could determine the level of supply chain collaboration of a SME with trading partners.

articleTitle: Best practice: An optimization of assets productivity in semiconductor manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: ROE (Return on Equity) is something that causes the most concern by stockholders and is a major index when evaluating a company's overall profitability. This paper introduces a new index-Equipment Asset Productivity (EAP) to aid index-Asset Productivity (AP), the key elements of ROE, by benchmarking Fab-by-Fab asset management performance over time. A hierarchical asset management mechanism was developed to identify the root causes of poor asset management performance. The aim is to provide attainable execution plan that will allow senior management to improve assets productivity. In addition, the paper also designates the ownership of each index required to monitor progress in the future then by raising ROE.

articleTitle: The long time lag between science and commercialization: The case of computers
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This paper analyzes a rarely addressed issue: the long time lag between scientific advances and the commercialization of them. Using the history of computers, it shows that the long time lag between advances in science (in the form of the concepts and architectures) and the implementation of them in the form of technological discontinuities was primarily due to inadequate components.

articleTitle: Analysis on human resource development through team activities
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: This study analyzed the human resource development through team activities. First, the paper reviewed existing studies on capability and skill model, and reconstructed an appropriate capability model for analysis on team activities. The study used 156 cases of QC circles. The text data of 156 cases were classified utilizing the method of text mining and key words could be extracted. Through clustering these key words, the model of three elements on capability were found. By using this model, it is possible to explain the capability as numerical data, and the management based on statistical analysis can be adopted. In addition, it can be expected to contribute to the decision making on the management to attempt appropriate promotion of team activities.

articleTitle: An algorithm for quality control charts for autocorrelated data
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Currently considerable attention has been given to the effect of data correlation on statistical process control (SPC). Use of traditional SPC methods when observations are correlated often leads to misleading conclusions as to whether or not the process is under control. The objective of this paper is to develop an algorithm to adjust a model ARMA(p,q), for calculate the run length distribution (RLD), the average run length (ARL), and the standard deviation of the run length (SRL), for residual control charts X(ind) and MR used to monitor autocorrelated processes. The algorithm was used for analysis of real data. We conclude that for negative first-order autocorrelation, the residuals chart is performing better than the Shewhart chart for independent observations.

articleTitle: Managing sustainability for the development of sustainable recycling technologies
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Brought into focus by sustainable development along with related issues of resource efficiency and health hazard reduction, sustainability in industrial waste recycling is becoming an emerging area with potentials to contribute to environmental protection, economic development and social benefit. This paper examines a sustainability management approach to the development of sustainable recycling technologies. It focuses on characterizing, modeling and assessing the critical sustainability factors of a closed-loop recycling technology for recovery of nickel from waste catalysts. The sustainability factors are identified from the nickel recovery process and modeled in metrics to evaluate economic and environmental impacts. The results suggest that the economic profitability of nickel recovery from wastes strongly depends on nickel market values and it also increases over production batch size. Its environmental impact is highly sensitive to changes in energy consumption. However, energy intensity indicates that there exist improvement rooms in energy efficiency for the current process.

articleTitle: Research on failure model of software reliability based on the least squares support vector regression machines and simulated annealing algorithm
publicationTitle: 2010 IEEE International Conference on Management of Innovation & Technology
abstract: Building a software failure model (SFM) is an important means to compute the software reliability. While there are not enough faults data, the estimation for model parameters is not accurate, which would decrease the fitting precision. In addition, the estimation for parameters of complex models is very complicated. An SFM based on the least squares support vector regression machines (LSSVRM) could decrease the fitting error, and there are no parameters to estimate in that SFM.
